tips.title: How to photograph your mini
tips.raking: Raking side light matters most: light the mini from one side at about 45° so the sculpt casts soft shadows. That shading is what the tool reads.
tips.no_flash: No frontal flash. A flash pointing straight at the mini fills the recesses and flattens the form — the #1 cause of a flat result.
tips.fill: Fill the frame: get close (or crop) so the mini takes up most of the photo.
tips.background: Use a plain, neutral background so the mini is easy to separate.
tips.focus: Keep it sharp: focus on the mini and use a timer or brace your hands.
tips.primed: Black or grey primer works best — the tool reads the lighting, so a raking side light matters more than the primer colour.
tips.painted: On an already painted mini the automatic check can't tell flash from good lighting, so a raking side light matters even more.

quality.title: This photo may give weaker results
quality.lighting: Lighting looks flat — use one raking light from the side (~45°) and turn off any flash.
quality.exposure: Part of the mini is crushed to black or blown out — adjust exposure or diffuse the light.
quality.focus: The photo looks soft — refocus on the mini and hold steady (use a timer).
quality.resolution: The mini is small in the frame — move closer or crop so it fills most of the photo.
quality.input: No mini detected — try a plainer background or a different photo.
